record.paper_title: Invitation to H-systems in higher dimensions: known results, new facts, and related open problems
record.original_question: Let u be in W^{1,n}(B^n,R^m) and suppose u satisfies the degenerate n-Laplace system -div(|grad u|^{n-2} grad u) = Omega · |grad u|^{n-2} grad u on B^n. Assume Omega=(Omega^alpha_ij) belongs to L^n(R^{m by m} tensor R^n) and is antisymmetric in the target indices, meaning Omega^alpha_ij = -Omega^alpha_ji for all i and j. Does this antisymmetric-potential structure force u to be continuous?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.5. Let u ∈ W 1,n (B n , Rm ) satisfy a system of the form − div |∇u|n−2 ∇u = Ω · |∇u|n−2 ∇u.
Assume that Ω = (Ωαij ) ∈ L n (Rm×m ⊗ Rn ) is antisymmetric, i.e. Ωαij = −Ωαji for all 1 ≤ i, j ≤ m. Is it true that u is continuous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and $m \geq 1$ be integers, and let $B^n \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ denote the open unit ball. Consider a map $u \in W^{1,n}(B^n,\mathbb{R}^m)$ that is a (distributional) solution of the degenerate $n$-Laplace system
$$-\operatorname{div} igl(|
abla u|^{n-2}\,
abla u igr) \;=\; \Omega \cdot |
abla u|^{n-2}\,
abla u \qquad 	ext{in } B^n,$$
where the right-hand side is interpreted componentwise as
$$ igl(\Omega \cdot |
abla u|^{n-2}\,
abla u igr)^i \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{\alpha=1}^{n} \Omega^{\alpha}_{ij}\,|
abla u|^{n-2}\,\partial_\alpha u^j, \qquad i=1,\dots,m.$$
Assume that the coefficient field $\Omega = (\Omega^{\alpha}_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le m,\,1\le\alpha\le n}$ belongs to $L^{n}(B^n,\,\mathbb{R}^{m	imes m}\otimes\mathbb{R}^n)$ and is antisymmetric in the target indices, i.e.
$$\Omega^{\alpha}_{ij} \;=\; -\,\Omega^{\alpha}_{ji} \qquad 	ext{for all } 1\le i,j \le m 	ext{ and all } 1\le \alpha \le n.$$
Does this antisymmetric structure of $\Omega$ imply that $u$ is continuous on $B^n$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is open in full generality. Under the additional assumption that $\Omega$ (or $\nabla u$) lies in a suitable Lorentz space (e.g. $L^{n,2}$), continuity of $u$ has been established via a Coulomb-gauge rotation of the system together with Iwaniec stability and Lorentz-space gradient estimates. The case of merely $L^n$ antisymmetric potentials, however, has not been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Regularizing properties of n-Laplace systems with antisymmetric potentials in Lorentz spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Continuity of solutions to n-Laplace systems with antisymmetric potential under Lorentz-space assumptions; introduces a Coulomb gauge and Lorentz-space gradient estimates.
status_evidence.claim: Continuity is known under stronger Lorentz-space hypotheses, not under merely L^n antisymmetric potentials.

status_evidence.title: Regularizing properties of n-Laplace systems with antisymmetric potentials in Lorentz spaces (Math. Ann.)
status_evidence.snippet: As a corollary, n-harmonic maps are continuous if their gradient belongs to L^{n,2}, the weakest assumption to date.
status_evidence.claim: The continuity result requires a Lorentz-space refinement beyond plain L^n; the unrefined problem remains open.
